COMPONENT KIT

  • Goo filter — feGaussianBlur + feColorMatrix alpha threshold that makes neighbouring circles fuse
  • Droplet — circle with an off-centre radial gradient and a separate specular highlight
  • Channel — a rounded track each metric's drops flow down
  • Merge pool — the calm body of all healthy metrics
  • Rogue bead — the coral drop that will not merge, with ripple rings — the anomaly
  • Label chip — mono text and the anomaly card kept outside the filter so they stay crisp

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Path flow — drops follow the channel path, power1.in, 0.06 s stagger; one release per beat at 120 BPM
  • Merge snap — the neck stretches for 2 frames, then fuses with elastic.out(1, .4) 0.6 s, landing on a downbeat
  • Repel wobble — the coral bead squashes ±8 % in a 3-cycle damped sine (0.5 s) on the snare when it refuses to merge

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Surface tension is an instant visual for “this doesn't belong”: everyone understands a drop that won't join the rest. It feels alive but contained. Risk: the goo filter blurs anything inside it, so every word and number must live outside the filtered group.

Adapt to your product: Make each drop one unit of your product's flow (orders, events, jobs) and the pool the healthy total; the thing your product catches is the drop that won't merge. Keep all labels as crisp overlays.

References: https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/06/09/how-to-create-interactive-droplet-like-metaballs-with-three-js-and-glsl/ (droplet metaballs with Three.js and GLSL) · https://css-tricks.com/gooey-effect/ (the SVG gooey filter technique)
